findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project IDs, which is not stable or collision-free
findings.body: hash(tuple(...)) of ints is deterministic within a process, but a 64-bit hash makes collisions possible. Two different project sets could then share an eligibility result, so a non-allowlisted project could be upsampled, or the reverse. The key is built from the hash instead of the joined IDs, so it is not safe as a cross-process cache key. Build the key from the joined sorted IDs instead.

findings.title: Cache invalidation is never called, so the cache is stale for up to 60s
findings.body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but nothing calls it, and it only deletes a single project-set key. Changes to the allowlist option therefore do not take effect until the 60s TTL expires. The docstring claiming consistency is misleading. The caching also saves almost nothing, because options.get is already cheap.

findings.title: Transform only handles an exact 'count()' and always aliases the result as 'count'
findings.body: Other count forms and aggregates are not handled, such as count() with an alias, or equations. Rewriting to 'upsampled_count() as count' can also collide with a user-requested column that is already named count. Events lacking sample_weight (older events, or events without a client sample rate) would sum to 0, so the chart would undercount. The comments claim the schema guarantees the column, but nothing enforces that.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses the outer dataset and request query rather than the scoped dataset and actual query
findings.body: The check passes the closure's `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`, and it inspects request.GET['query'] instead of the `query` parameter. The dashboard-widget split paths call _get_event_stats with discover and a rewritten query such as '!event.type:transaction'. In those paths the decision is wrong, so transaction queries could get upsampled_count (sample_weight does not exist for transactions), or error queries could be missed. The check is also repeated on every call. Also, 'event.type:error' is matched as a substring of the query text, which misses queries like '!event.type:error' and similar forms.

findings.title: Upsampling is applied to RPC datasets, but the transform produces a legacy-only function
findings.body: In the RPC paths (spans_rpc and ourlogs), the transform emits 'upsampled_count() as count'. This is only defined in the discover SnQL function converter. The helper returns False for those datasets, so the path is dead code today, but it would break if the helper changes.

findings.title: upsampled_count is registered as a public function for all discover queries
findings.body: It is not marked private. Users can call it directly against transactions or non-allowlisted projects, where sample_weight is missing, and get errors or wrong results. It also sums sample_weight without the sampling-rate inversion (1/rate), so the semantics are unclear.

findings.title: Tests mock the whole options module and depend on factory behavior, with no cache coverage
findings.body: Mocking `options` makes every options.get return the allowlist, which affects unrelated lookups. The cache is never cleared between tests, and the key is identical for identical project sets, so tests can leak state. The caching, the invalidate function, and the top_events path are untested.

findings.title: Test factory silently swallows all exceptions and rewrites sample_rate for all store_event callers
findings.body: The bare `except Exception: pass` blocks hide errors. The helper also changes sample_rate for any test event that carries the error_sampling context, a global change to fixtures. Also, a client_sample_rate of 0 is ignored because the check is truthiness.

findings.title: Stray submodule/gitlink file added to the PR
findings.body: The 'sentry-repo' file is a subproject commit pointer unrelated to the feature. It should not be committed.
